es.summary: Descenso de la vejiga, útero o recto hacia la vagina por debilitamiento del suelo pélvico.
key_points: Se clasifica según el órgano prolapsado: cistocele, rectocele, prolapso uterino o entero.
Factores de riesgo principales: embarazo, parto vaginal, obesidad y envejecimiento.
Síntomas incluyen sensación de peso, protrusión vaginal y pérdida de orina o heces.
El diagnóstico se confirma con examen pélvico y, de ser necesario, ecografía o cistouretrografía.
El manejo incluye ejercicios de Kegel, pesario y, en casos graves, cirugía reparadora.

pathophysiology: El suelo pélvico pierde tono y soporte por daño muscular o de tejido conectivo.
Los órganos pélvicos pierden su posición anatómica y empujan contra la pared vaginal.
La presión intraabdominal aumenta la protrusión durante tos, esfuerzo o al final del día.
signs_symptoms: Sensación de pesadez o plenitud vaginal.
Protrusión visible o palpable en la vagina.
Incontinencia urinaria de esfuerzo o urgencia.
Incontinencia fecal o dificultad para evacuar.
Dolor o molestia durante relaciones sexuales.
diagnostics: Examen pélvico con maniobras de Valsalva para observar el grado de prolapso.
Ecografía transvaginal o pélvica para evaluar posición de órganos.
Cistouretrografía o urodinámica si hay síntomas urinarios.
Escala POP-Q (Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification) para clasificar gravedad.
treatment: Ejercicios de Kegel y fisioterapia del suelo pélvico.
Uso de pesario vaginal de silicona o látex.
Laxantes suaves (docusato) para evitar esfuerzo durante la defecación.
Cirugía reparadora (colporrafia, sacrocolpopexia) en grados III‑IV.
complications: Úlceras por presión en la zona de protrusión.
Disfunción sexual y disminución de la calidad de vida.
Obstrucción intestinal en casos de rectocele severo.
nursing_care: Evaluar grado de prolapso y síntomas urinarios/fecales en cada turno.
Registrar ingesta y eliminación; vigilar signos de retención urinaria.
Enseñar técnica correcta de ejercicios de Kegel y uso del pesario.
Mantener higiene perineal adecuada para prevenir infecciones.
Posicionar a la paciente con rodillas flexionadas y evitar levantar objetos pesados.
patient_teaching: Practicar ejercicios de Kegel 3 veces al día, 10 repeticiones cada vez.
Evitar estreñimiento: dieta rica en fibra (25‑30 g/día) y 2 L de agua.
Uso y cuidado del pesario: limpieza diaria y revisión médica cada 6‑12 meses.
Controlar peso corporal y evitar el sobreesfuerzo abdominal.
Buscar atención médica ante aumento de la protrusión o infecciones urinarias.

outcomes: Nivel de actividad: la paciente realizará al menos el 80 % de sus actividades de vida diaria sin dolor en 2 semanas.
Fatiga: la paciente reportará disminución de la sensación de cansancio a <3/10 en escala de dolor en 1 semana.

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de dolor y capacidad funcional antes y después de cada actividad.
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar el plan de ejercicios y prevenir sobrecarga.

interventions.action: Enseñar y supervisar ejercicios de Kegel y respiración diafragmática.
interventions.rationale: Fortalece el suelo pélvico y reduce la fatiga al disminuir el esfuerzo.

interventions.action: Planificar actividades en bloques de 10‑15 min con descansos de 5 min.
interventions.rationale: Distribuye la carga física y evita la intolerancia al esfuerzo prolongado.

interventions.action: Fomentar una dieta alta en fibra y adecuada hidratación.
interventions.rationale: Previene el estreñimiento y reduce el esfuerzo durante la defecación.

interventions.action: Coordinar con fisioterapeuta para programa de fortalecimiento del suelo pélvico.
interventions.rationale: Mejora el soporte estructural y disminuye la limitación funcional.

related_to: úlceras por presión en zona de protrusión
outcomes: Sin signos de infección del tracto urinario (ausencia de fiebre, disuria) durante la hospitalización.
Piel perineal intacta y sin erythema en 48 horas.

interventions.action: Realizar higiene perineal cuidadosa después de cada micción o evacuación.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la colonización bacteriana y previene infecciones.

interventions.action: Inspeccionar diariamente la zona del pesario y la piel perineal.
interventions.rationale: Detecta irritación o úlceras tempranas para intervención oportuna.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente el método correcto de inserción y extracción del pesario.
interventions.rationale: Minimiza traumatismo y contaminación del dispositivo.

interventions.action: Promover ingesta adecuada de líquidos (≥2 L/día) para favorecer la micción frecuente.
interventions.rationale: Ayuda a eliminar bacterias del tracto urinario.

interventions.action: Notificar al médico ante cualquier signo de infección (fiebre, disuria, leucocitosis).
interventions.rationale: Permite iniciar tratamiento antibiótico precoz.

en.summary: Descent of the bladder, uterus, or rectum into the vagina due to pelvic floor weakening.
key_points: It is classified by the prolapsed organ: cystocele, rectocele, uterine prolapse, or enterocele.
Main risk factors: pregnancy, vaginal delivery, obesity, and aging.
Symptoms include a feeling of weight, vaginal protrusion, and urinary or fecal incontinence.
Diagnosis is confirmed with a pelvic exam and, if necessary, ultrasound or cystourethrography.
Management includes Kegel exercises, pessary use, and, in severe cases, reconstructive surgery.

pathophysiology: The pelvic floor loses tone and support due to muscle or connective tissue damage.
Pelvic organs lose their anatomical position and push against the vaginal wall.
Intraabdominal pressure increases protrusion during coughing, straining, or at the end of the day.
signs_symptoms: Feeling of heaviness or fullness in the vagina.
Visible or palpable protrusion in the vagina.
diagnostics: Pelvic exam with Valsalva maneuvers to assess prolapse degree.
Transvaginal or pelvic ultrasound to evaluate organ position.
Cystourethrography or urodynamics if urinary symptoms are present.
POP‑Q (Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification) scale to classify severity.
treatment: Kegel exercises and pelvic floor physical therapy.
Use of a silicone or latex vaginal pessary.
Gentle laxatives (docusate) to avoid straining during defecation.
Reconstructive surgery (colporrhaphy, sacrocolpopexy) for stages III‑IV.
complications: Pressure ulcers at the protrusion site.
Sexual dysfunction and reduced quality of life.
Intestinal obstruction in severe rectocele cases.
nursing_care: Assess prolapse degree and urinary/fecal symptoms each shift.
Record intake and elimination; monitor for urinary retention signs.
Teach correct Kegel technique and pessary use.
Maintain proper perineal hygiene to prevent infections.
Position the patient with knees flexed and avoid lifting heavy objects.
patient_teaching: Practice Kegel exercises 3 times daily, 10 repetitions each time.
Avoid constipation: diet rich in fiber (25‑30 g/day) and 2 L of water.
Use and care for the pessary: daily cleaning and medical review every 6‑12 months.
Monitor body weight and avoid abdominal overexertion.
Seek medical attention if protrusion increases or urinary infections occur.

outcomes: Activity level: the patient will perform at least 80% of her activities of daily living without pain in 2 weeks.
Fatigue: the patient will report a decrease in fatigue to <3/10 on the pain scale in 1 week.

interventions.action: Assess pain level and functional capacity before and after each activity.
interventions.rationale: Allows adjustment of the exercise plan and prevents overload.

interventions.action: Teach and supervise Kegel and diaphragmatic breathing exercises.
interventions.rationale: Strengthens the pelvic floor and reduces fatigue by decreasing effort.

interventions.action: Plan activities in 10‑15 minute blocks with 5 minute breaks.
interventions.rationale: Distributes physical load and avoids intolerance to prolonged effort.

interventions.action: Encourage a high-fiber diet and adequate hydration.
interventions.rationale: Prevents constipation and reduces straining during defecation.

interventions.action: Coordinate with a physiotherapist for a pelvic floor strengthening program.
interventions.rationale: Improves structural support and decreases functional limitation.

outcomes: No signs of urinary tract infection (absence of fever, dysuria) during hospitalization.
Intact perineal skin without erythema within 48 hours.

interventions.action: Perform careful perineal hygiene after each void or evacuation.
interventions.rationale: Reduces bacterial colonization and prevents infections.

interventions.action: Inspect the pessary area and perineal skin daily.
interventions.rationale: Detects early irritation or ulcers for timely intervention.

interventions.action: Teach the patient the correct method of pessary insertion and removal.
interventions.rationale: Minimizes trauma and contamination of the device.

interventions.action: Promote adequate fluid intake (≥2 L/day) to encourage frequent voiding.
interventions.rationale: Helps eliminate bacteria from the urinary tract.

interventions.action: Notify the physician of any infection signs (fever, dysuria, leukocytosis).
interventions.rationale: Allows early initiation of antibiotic treatment.

key_points.2.quote: Symptoms of uterine prolapse include urinary incontinence, feeling of fullness in the vagina, bulging of the vagina, constipation, and back pain.

key_points.4.quote: Other potential treatments include pelvic floor strengthening exercises, bladder training, hormone replacement therapy, wearing a pessary , or surgical repair.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Relaxation of the pelvic floor muscles and connective tissue can cause the organs to sag ( pelvic organ prolapse ) and can interfere with their function, causing pain, leaking of urine or stool, constipation, feelings of fullness in the vagina, and difficulty in defecating.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Factors that increase the incidence of pelvic floor disorders include pregnancy, increased parity (the number of deliveries), vaginal delivery, connective tissue disorders, and health conditions that cause chronic coughing (ACOG, 2019).

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Common symptoms include: Feeling heaviness, fullness, pulling, or aching in the vagina.

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: Other symptoms a patient may present with are pelvic pain and discomfort with penetrative vaginal intercourse.
